## 分诊 · `domain:devx` / `priority:p2` / `pm:blocked` (by #14147 / PR #15395)

**Anchor read, not guessed.** The deliverable is the subject set of two rules in `packages/lint/src/` (`validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts`, `validate-readonly-hook-writes.ts`) plus their pinning tests. Nothing lands in `packages/objectql` or `service-automation`. ⇒ `domain:devx`.

### The correction this card needs: it is a **future** defect, not a live one

Re-measured on `origin/main` `f1d7872` (2026-09-04T23:38:52Z). The card's body says the create-side no-op *"is now"* the behaviour — that is true of #14147's PR branch, and **not yet true of `main`**:

| read | result |
|---|---|
| `stripReadonlyForInsert` | 5 files, all still describing it as the **DataProtocol ingress** guard (`rule-validator.ts:1310`, `engine.ts:6062` — "#3043") |
| `stripReadonlyForInsert` called from `engine.insert` | **not present** |
| the superseded premise in the lint rules | still there verbatim — `validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts:14`, `validate-readonly-hook-writes.ts:42` |
| `READONLY_ACTION_INSERT_SILENCE` (the action-sibling pin the card says is "already handled") | **0 hits repo-wide** |
| positive control for that zero | the same sweep returns `READONLY_ACTION_WRITE_EXCLUSIONS`, `READONLY_ACTION_WRITE_PATTERN_IDS`, `READONLY_HOOK_WRITE_EXCLUSIONS`, `READONLY_HOOK_WRITE_PATTERN_IDS`, `READONLY_FIELD`, `READONLY_WHEN_FIELD` ⇒ the pin token's absence is real, not a broken pattern |
| #14147 | `pm:dispatched`, assigned, **PR #15395 open** — "a static `readonly` field is stripped from a non-system INSERT inside `engine.insert`, and the boundary copy is deleted" |

So today a non-system flow `create_record` still **lands** the readonly value (the flow engine calls the data engine directly and bypasses the ingress copy) — which is exactly what the rules' current comment says, and why they are correct as written *right now*. The moment PR #15395 merges, that comment becomes false and the scan gap becomes a live silent no-op.

That is not a criticism of the filing — the dev measured against the branch it was working in and said so. It changes only *when* this is actionable, which is why it goes to `pm:blocked` rather than `pm:queue`: **shipping the widened rules before #15395 would emit error-severity findings about writes that currently land.** A false `error` on a build is worse than the gap it closes.

**Blocked-by: #14147 (PR #15395). Unblocks automatically on that merge — no ruling needed to start.**

### Grade — p2

Not p1: it needs a non-elevated flow or hook that seeds a readonly column, and after #15395 the run still emits a step warning naming the dropped field, so the information exists — just at run time, days later, in a WARN log. Not p3: this rule family's entire stated purpose is shifting that discovery **left** to `os validate` / `os build` (#3425), so a create-verb gap is the rule failing at its own job on the sibling verb, not a nice-to-have.

### Boundary test — Bug, and no manual floor

Widening the subject set **narrows** the accept set: it makes illegal a shape the engine will (post-#15395) already refuse to honour. That is restoring declared = enforced, not a feature, and gate *strengthening* is not the gate-weakening case that sits above the manual floor. Ordinary lane work.

⚠️ **But the landing plan is part of the card, not a side effect** — the filer is right and this is the sentence that pins it. Before the widened rules land, measure the blast radius on in-repo flows and hooks: any that seed a readonly column on create without elevation red the build the day this ships. Expected count is a deliverable of this card. The same pass must flip the two tests that currently pin the old premise as correct behaviour — `validate-readonly-flow-writes.test.ts:327` ("clean: create_record is engine-exempt from the readonly strip") and `validate-readonly-hook-writes.test.ts:215` ("GREEN: INSERT is engine-exempt") — plus `validate-flow-node-writes.test.ts:409`, which the card does not list and which asserts the same thing from a third file.

### Two constraints carried forward, both endorsed

1. **Static shape only, on the create verb.** `readonlyWhen` has no create-side strip — `engine.ts:11592` still reads "single-id `stripReadonlyWhenFields`; INSERT stays exempt" — so a conditional finding on a create would state something false. Keep the `runAs:'system'` / elevation exemption gating the static branch exactly as it does on update.
2. **`validate-readonly-action-writes.ts` is out of scope and must stay out.** An action body is `{ ...ec, isSystem: true }` by construction, so a static-`readonly` finding there would be false about a write that lands. Its silence is a reasoned refusal, and its pin should land with #15395 — if that pin does not exist when this card is taken, say so on #14147 rather than adding it here.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

Correction to a sentence in this card's body — "The prose in both files has been corrected in #14147's PR" — which was **not true** at PR #15395's head `bd598e803`, and which PR #15395's own body repeated.

Measured at that head: only the hook rule's header (`packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-hook-writes.ts:39-52`) had been rewritten. The flow rule's header (`validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts:14-18`) still read "INSERT is engine-exempt from the readonly strip … so a create writing a readonly field is NOT a no-op and is never flagged"; the hook rule's `STRIP_SUBJECT_METHODS` docblock (`:209-212`) still read "absent BY DECISION, not by omission: the engine exempts INSERT"; and the GREEN control blocks in `validate-readonly-hook-writes.test.ts:215` and `validate-readonly-flow-writes.test.ts:327` (plus a third in `validate-flow-node-writes.test.ts:409`) still justified themselves with the overturned sentence.

The patch round on PR #15395 (commits `b5fb6d728` and `da62e0e93`, head `66c580b0c`) corrects all of them: both rules' docblocks now name the `insert`/`create` silence as a scan gap that this card owns rather than an exemption, and the green cases keep their verdicts with the reason restated — "the conditional lock has no prior record on a create; the static half is the #15394 gap" — so that when this card lands they flip to red for the static shape instead of sitting green on a false premise. The scan gap itself is untouched by that PR and remains this card's deliverable.

The scan-gap widening itself is untouched on `main` — that is this card's deliverable. ⚠️ Widening two rules to report a non-system `create_record` / `ctx.api.insert` of a `readonly` column at **error** severity changes what `os lint` accepts ⇒ the dispatch will declare `Clause-②: yes` and run at the contract-review tier (or carry `needs:contract-review` if that tier is exhausted). `packages/lint` is serial — one lint card in flight at a time.

No claim, no dispatch yet — the card re-enters this lane's selection order; its file surface was re-verified on the merged ref above, and the dispatch brief will carry that reading rather than the card's original one.
